messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — GPU cluster 'infer-west-2' autoscaler unhealthy. queue_length=12,400 (+4k in 5m), node_util=98%, failover candidates exhausted. paging oncall.

sophia: paging @oncall (raj) — we have large queue growth and 5% increase in 429s in prod. customers hitting timeouts. any initial triage?

raj: looking. I can see the HPA metrics for the gpu-deployments are stuck — custom metrics lagging. prometheus-adapter shows >2m scrape latency and lots of 500s to the metrics API.

kim: confirming frontend alarms: 429 spikes from model-infer endpoints. Customer-impact dashboard shows increased error rate for tiered customers in us-west-2. Noticed kube-apiserver metrics delayed too.

sophia: initial impact — degraded throughput for live inference, fallback to smaller model is firing but not enough. severity=P1. starting live mitigation checklist.

raj: immediate mitigation options: 1) manually scale GPU autoscaler target (bypass HPA) 2) re-route traffic to other regions 3) restart prometheus-adapter/metrics-server. Which first?

james: I'm available to take over handoff. I'll coordinate infra for restarts. @sophia can you capture current outputs so we have an audit trail before we restart anything?

sophia: copying commands:
```
# current HPA targets
kubectl get hpa -n inference --selector=app=model-infer -o wide
# adapter logs
kubectl logs -n monitoring deploy/prometheus-adapter --tail=200
```

sophia: pasted last 10 lines of adapter logs:
```
E0321 12:03:10 adapter.go:214] error querying custom metrics: timeout
E0321 12:03:11 adapter.go:214] error querying custom metrics: connection refused
E0321 12:03:12 adapter.go:214] error querying custom metrics: upstream 502
```

infra-bot: scheduled restart of deployment/prometheus-adapter in namespace monitoring (requested by james). rolling restart started — pods terminating. pod/prom-adapter-5 -> Terminating.

raj: while adapter recovers, we should also manually scale critical GPU replica sets to prevent customer timeouts. Proposing: scale model-infer-critical to +3 replicas (temp).

james: running manual scale now:
`kubectl scale deploy/model-infer-critical --replicas=6 -n inference`

sophia: :thumbsup: manual scale applied. note: this will temporarily increase cost.

pagerduty: Incident INC-54321 assigned to raj and james. Priority: P1. Paging policy: escalate in 5m if not acked.

kim: traffic reroute: enabling soft-failover to eu-west-1 for non-enterprise customers to reduce pressure; enterprise customers pinned to us-west-2 (they're affected). Starting traffic shift for ~30% of requests.

raj: prometheus-adapter pods are back up but logs show scrape backlog being replayed. adapter reports some stale metrics dropped. HPA controllers read custom metrics every 30s; we might see lag for ~2 minutes.

sophia: monitoring: queue length dropped from 12.4k -> 7.1k after manual scale + reroute. 429s decreased from 8.3% -> 4.2%. good sign but still above SLO.

james: next step: investigate root cause of adapter backlog — quick checks: Prometheus scrape queue (disk IO?), API rate limits, and network latency to prometheus. Can someone check prom-scrape-latency and prometheus CPU?

kim: prometheus CPU spike at time of incident: 95% for 10m, disk i/o high on pvc-prom-main-1. Looks like compaction/backfill running.

raj: that explains backlog. If compaction is a recurring maintenance job, we need better coordination with autoscale. For now, let's create a short-term rule to prefer metrics from metrics-server/kube-state when custom metrics are unavailable.

sophia: implemented fallback policy in routing: if custom-metrics lag >60s, autoscaler uses proxy KPIs (queue_per_pod) for decisions. Pushing as emergency config change.

james: applied emergency config to autoscaler controller: `--enable-fallback-metrics=true` and restarted autoscaler controller-manager.

infra-bot: restart acknowledged for controller-manager; new pod healthy.

sophia: post-mitigation status: queue down to 2.3k, 429s at 1.1% and latency nearing normal. Manual scale to be tapered once HPA catches up.

kim: customer comms: drafting interim status to affected enterprise customers explaining degradation, mitigation, and ETA for full remediation.

raj: timeline & next actions:
- 12:03 root cause: Prometheus compaction/backfill caused scrape IO spike -> adapter backlog -> HPA lag -> queue growth
- 12:12 manual scale + reroute reduced immediate customer impact
- 12:22 restarted prometheus-adapter + autoscaler fallback -> HPA resumed reading metrics
- 12:40 plan: schedule Prometheus maintenance window, add autoscaler fallback permanently, add alert for prom compaction >60s

james: taking post-incident owner. I'll write the incident doc and schedule follow-ups with infra and storage team. handing back to oncall rotation (raj) in 15m.

sophia: handing off remaining monitoring to raj. thanks everyone. :pray:

raj: ack — I'll remain on watch for 1hr. adding steps to postmortem checklist and tagging storage infra.

incident-bot: Incident INC-54321 status updated to mitigation_in_progress -> monitoring. next update expected by 13:00.
